title: docs: board auto-adds issues; document the sub-issue-per-PR pattern
body:
## Why

`dev/guides/tracking-work.md` and `AGENTS.md` said every new issue must be added to the board by hand with `gh project item-add`. The board's built-in **Auto-add to project** workflow now does that.

Closes #151

## What Changed

- **`dev/guides/tracking-work.md`**:
  - The new "Adding issues to the board" section describes the Auto-add workflow (`anton-tvrz/snapl`, `is:issue,pr is:open`) and the Item closed → Done workflow.
  - It explains that auto-add doesn't backfill, so older issues are added from the sidebar or with `gh project item-add`, and that the command needs the `project` token scope.
  - It says what to check if an issue doesn't appear.
  - The SDD bullet now explains why every PR, spec PRs included, needs its own sub-issue under the umbrella: PR validation requires `Closes #N`. #148 and #150 under #101 are the examples.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: the work-tracking line matches.

## How to Review

- **Merge only after the Auto-add workflow is turned on** on the board (**⋯ → Workflows → Auto-add to project**). Until then, the guide's claim isn't true (ADR-0004).
- After merging, #146 and #147 still need adding by hand, because auto-add doesn't backfill.

## How to Test

Docs only. After turning the workflow on, file any issue in snapl and check that it appears on https://github.com/users/anton-tvrz/projects/4 within a minute.

## Impact & Rollout

- [x] Backward compatible
- [x] No new dependencies
- [x] No config changes required

## TDD Checklist

- [ ] Tests written before implementation (TDD): n/a, docs only
- [ ] All new source files have corresponding test files: n/a
- [ ] Failing test demonstrated before fix (bug fixes only): n/a
- [ ] Coverage threshold met on new code (>=80%): n/a

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added/updated: n/a
- [ ] Linting passes (`uv run ruff check .`): no Python changed
- [ ] Changelog fragment added (if user-facing change): docs only, `skip-changelog`
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)

title: docs(knowledge): SR Linux WAN overlay spike — EVPN-VXLAN, not GRE
body:
Closes #134
Refs #126 (the WAN feature issue stays open)

## What this is

This is the tunnel spike from decision 1 in #126. It is docs and fixtures only: no source code, and the companion doc is left as it is.

- `dev/knowledge/sr-linux-wan-overlay.md`: the questions, the evidence, the YANG paths, the recommendation and what wasn't verified.
- `tests/fixtures/srlinux_wan_overlay/`: real SR Linux 26.3.1 gNMI Set payloads and GET responses, with a README. No test reads them yet. That's why they're in their own directory and not under a package's fixtures.

## Findings (live lab, `ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux:26.3.1`, `ixr-d3`)

- **GRE and IP-in-IP are out.** SR Linux has no GRE or IP-in-IP *interface*. GRE exists only as a static next-hop-group encap. That encap is limited to 7250 IXR models, and the YANG forbids BFD on it. On IXR-D3 the feature is absent, and a gNMI Set was rejected (`no local leaf with the name 'encapsulate-header'`).
- **VXLAN works, with EVPN only.** The source is always `system0`, so each hub/branch pair gets one tunnel, not one per underlay. Underlay routing chooses the path: one eBGP + BFD session per underlay, with local-pref deciding which one carries the remote VTEP `/32`.
- **gNMI:** each node's whole config went on in one `set(update=[("/", payload)])`, the Executor's own call.
- **Failover:** BGP moved to the second underlay with a **2.25–3.0 s** loss window. The EVPN overlay session never dropped. Recovery lost 0 packets.
- **BFD floor:** BFD runs at **1 s** in the container even when configured for 100 ms. That puts T-03's 2000 ms target out of reach in this lab.
- **netem** works on SR Linux interfaces, and the T-05 brownout gap reproduced live: BGP didn't move traffic off the degraded path.
- **eBGP + BFD inside the tunnel** (VRF loopbacks over VXLAN) works, but it flapped once during underlay failover.

The `wan-spike` lab was throwaway: mgmt `172.20.30.0/24`, network `clab-wan-spike`. It was destroyed after the run. dcfabric and the compose stack were not touched.

## Test plan

- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (check-json, detect-secrets, gitleaks)
- [x] Every committed payload was captured from, or accepted by, a live SR Linux 26.3.1 node

title: docs(spec): 008-site-edge — a segmentation rule as intent
body:
## Summary

Spec and plan for the **site_edge** use case (Refs #117): an SR Linux site edge with office, OT and WAN segments, and an SR Linux carrier over eBGP. Its intent holds one segmentation rule, an ingress ACL on the OT interface: accept to one named subnet, drop everything else. Removing or weakening that rule by hand is drift that `snapl scan` reports and `snapl reconcile` restores.

Docs only: `specs/008-site-edge/` (spec, plan, research, data-model, contracts, quickstart, checklist). Nothing is implemented. Per #117 this is built **after #103** ships, which is still open.

Closes #132

Refs #117, which stays open for the implementation.

## Answer these three over coffee

These are the spec's `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers, verbatim. Each has a proposed default, and the plan is written against those defaults. research.md says exactly what changes for each other answer.

1. **FR-014 (Q1)**: the WAN uplink goes over eBGP to "[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: one carrier router, or two (the site edge dual-homed to two carriers)?]"
   **Proposed: one.** A second carrier adds one interface, one eBGP session and one link. It shows nothing new about drift, and without failover verification it would be an implied claim. Adding it later touches only the seed, the topology and the guard test (R17).

2. **FR-017 (Q2)**: "Verification of the site_edge use case MUST [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: include the behavioural traffic test of User Story 5 (Linux hosts in the lab; OT can reach the allowed subnet and nothing else across the WAN), or is the first cut config-level only, with User Story 5 as a follow-on?]"
   **Proposed: follow-on.** It needs routed forwarding, which the current templates do not render:
   - subinterfaces in the network-instance
   - BGP import and export policy
   It also needs those as intent, plus hosts, plus confirmation that the virtual dataplane enforces ACLs (R18).

3. **FR-016 (Q3)**: for an ACL entry on the device but absent from intent, inside a snapl-declared ACL (the hand-inserted permit), reconcile MUST "[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: remove it in this feature? That would pull targeted removal of undesired config forward from #65 for snapl-owned ACLs only: dry-run first, operator-confirmed, never against the protected set (Principle VIII.5). Or only report it, leaving removal to #65?]"
   **Proposed: report only.** Removal needs a new `Executor` write path (an ABC change), a confirmation flow and its own live evidence. That is roughly the size of this feature again (R11, contracts/site-edge.md, last section).

**Also for you: spec number 008.** A local branch, `008-scheduled-drift-scans`, is checked out in your main checkout. It holds the #126 WAN doc commit and no `specs/008-*` directory. I was told to use 008 for this spec, so I did. If that branch is meant to become spec 008, one of the two needs renumbering.

## Notable assumptions (all in spec.md "Assumptions" and research.md)

- **One rule, ingress, IPv4 prefixes only.** No protocol or port matching, egress, IPv6 or multiple ACLs. The rule is an ACL in intent, not a zone policy compiled into ACLs.
- **The rule is enforced as an ingress filter on the OT segment:** `10 accept OT→10.50.10.0/24`, then `20 drop any→any`. A side effect is that OT cannot reach the office segment either. If you want that path open, it is one more accept entry in the seed.
- **The lab seed writes "any" as an explicit `0.0.0.0/0`.** That way every in-place weakening is a value change that merge-only apply can heal. Capture C2 must confirm the device keeps it as written.
- **The carrier is in intent** and is deployed by snapl, the way dcfabric models its spines. Not realistic for a provider router, but it keeps one config path. The docs will say so.
- **Seed roles use existing schema choices.** The vendored device-role Dropdown has no `carrier`, so `carrier-a` seeds as `core` and `site-edge-01` as `edge`. The WAN uplink uses interface role `upstream`, a base choice. It may be overridden by the Batch 3 `InterfacePhysical.role` re-declaration; if so, a `wan` choice is added to the project file. That is unverified and listed under capture C7 (R20).
- **Unmanaged match criteria are not detected.** For example, a protocol or port hand-added to the deny entry narrows it without detection. This is a stated limitation.
- **The binding is its own entity kind** (`acl_binding`), not an `Interface` field. A filter bound by hand elsewhere then reads as undesired, not as unhealable forward drift.
- **The SoT schema is a new Batch 3 file, `network_acl.yml`.** I did not extend the `BusinessFirewallRuleSet` stub, which is reserved, and did not vendor the schema-library's `experimental/security` model, which is a firewall zone and policy model.
- **The diff gets composite keys.** `key_field` becomes `key_fields`. This is the only generalization, and the two-key ACL entry forces it.
- **`/acl` joins the global `DRIFT_PATHS`.** dcfabric collects it too. "Converged dcfabric still scans clean" is a success criterion (SC-005).
- **The templates are copied.** `templates/site_edge/` copies `interfaces.j2` and `bgp.j2` rather than adding a shared-template loader. The render→diff contract test is parametrized by use case to guard the copies.
- **The lab has its own /24:** `clab-snapl-site-edge` on `172.20.22.0/24` (`site-edge-01` .11, `carrier-a` .21). It is registered in the host-resource registry, so both labs can run at once. New names, addresses and ASNs avoid dcfabric and test_edge (`edge-01` is taken).
- **The lab tasks become use-case aware** (`dev.lab-deploy --use-case`). No CLI or workflow changes are needed.

## Things the desk research turned up that you may want to know

- **The SR Linux ACL YANG and JSON shape is not written as fact anywhere in this spec.** The plan's first step is eight live captures on 26.3.1 (research R16, plan "Live Evidence Required"), starting with the **factory `/acl` baseline**, which decides the protected set. Capture **C5** (whether merge replaces the `accept`/`drop` YANG choice) is the one result that could change the plan.
- **Schema readiness gap.** The readiness poll (#87) waits only on *extension attributes*, so brand-new node kinds would bring the seed race back. The plan extends it (R5).
- **Unverified observation, possibly worth its own issue.** The dcfabric templates render no network-instance interface membership and no BGP policy. If SR Linux needs those for sessions to establish, which I expect but have not confirmed, dcfabric's eBGP sessions may not be established today. Verification compares config only, so nothing would notice. I did not touch the lab to check.

## Process notes

- Branched from `main` by hand, as `008-site-edge`. `create-new-feature.sh` takes the highest number from `git branch -a` (line 118), so the local `008-scheduled-drift-scans` branch would have pushed it to 009.
- `setup-plan.sh` ran with `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY=specs/008-site-edge`, so `.specify/feature.json`, which still points at 004, was left alone. The 005–007 spec PRs did not update it either.
- ⚠️ **Before `/speckit-tasks`:** Spec Kit finds the feature directory from the env var first, then `.specify/feature.json`, then the branch name. `feature.json` still says `specs/004-observability-drift`, so a plain `/speckit-tasks` on this branch would write into **004's** folder and overwrite its `tasks.md`. Run it with `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY=specs/008-site-edge`, or point `feature.json` at 008 first. I left `feature.json` alone because another spec PR (009) may touch the same line tonight.
- I skipped `update-agent-context.sh` (the `CLAUDE.md` "Recent Changes" update). The 005, 006 and 007 spec commits did not update it either, and this adds no new technology.
- No live evidence: docs-only, and no boundary is touched. The lab, Docker, Infrahub and Temporal were not used.
- `/speckit-tasks` waits until Q1–Q3 are answered.
